rule.manualCheck: Student must select one specialization by the end of the sophomore year and complete 2 specialization electives from the undergraduate guide list. Specialization courses must be passed with a C or higher.
rule.text: Select one of four specializations (Circuits and VLSI; Communications, Signal Processing, and Networking; Nanoelectronics and Photonics; Power and Energy Systems), each requiring 2 elective courses. Acceptable electives are listed in the electrical engineering undergraduate guide.

requirements.sourceText: Students must select one of the four specializations listed below by the end of the sophomore year. Circuits and VLSI; Communications, Signal Processing, and Networking; Nanoelectronics and Photonics; Power and Energy Systems. Each specialization requires 2 elective courses. A list of acceptable electives can be found in the electrical engineering undergraduate guide.

requirements.label: ese-technical-electives

rule.manualCheck: Courses must not already be required for the ESE major or used to satisfy the chosen specialization.

requirements.sourceText: Students are required to take three ESE technical electives (3 or 4 credit courses) which can be any upper division (300 or 400 level) ESE courses not already required for the ESE major or used to satisfy the chosen specialization.

policies.sourceText: All courses taken for the major must be taken for a letter grade.

A grade of C or higher is required in the following courses: ESE 118, ESE 271, ESE 272, ESE 273, ESE 300, ESE 301, ESE 305, ESE 315, ESE 323, ESE 331, ESE 342, ESE 440, ESE 441, Two ESE Technical Electives, ESE Specialization Courses, AMS 151 and AMS 161 or MAT 131 and MAT 132, PHY 131, PHY 132, PHY 133, PHY 134.
Note: ESE 440 and ESE 441 are engineering design project courses that must be carried out at Stony Brook under the supervision of an Electrical and Computer Engineering faculty member.

exemptions.reason: CEAS majors are exempt from the LANG learning objective.

notes.text: Acceptance into the major: AOI and other CEAS students must apply by January 5 (Spring) or June 5 (Fall) and meet these requirements: at least 10 credits of required mathematics, physics, and ECE courses (excluding ESE 300 and ESE 301); a G.P.A. of 3.2 or higher in those courses with no more than one grade below B-; no required major course repeated; and course evaluations completed for transferred courses used to meet major requirements. Requirements must be completed within one year of enrolling in the first course that applies toward major entry. Non-CEAS students and double major applicants follow a separate, competitive process that does not guarantee acceptance.
All students are assigned a faculty advisor who consults on course selection, academic progress, and career preparation. Course selection may be made in consultation with a faculty advisor.

The grading section lists 'Two ESE Technical Electives' while the Electrical Engineering requirements text says three. The ESE technical electives requirement above follows the requirements text (three). The C-or-higher policy covers that requirement as a whole.

Honors Program in Electrical Engineering (not evaluated): apply at the end of the sophomore year with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.50 and a B or better in all major required courses (including math and physics). Graduation with departmental honors requires a cumulative GPA of 3.50 or higher, a B or better in major required courses, ESE 494 (1-credit seminar, B or better, junior year), ESE 495 (3-credit honors research project, B or better), and an honors thesis approved by a two-faculty committee.

Accelerated five-year BE/MS in Electrical Engineering (or Computer Engineering) (not evaluated): open to the top 10 to 20 percent of the junior class with a major GPA of at least 3.30. Two 300-level electives are replaced by two 500-level graduate courses, counting six graduate credits toward the undergraduate degree.

Sample sequence note: ESE 440 and ESE 441 partially satisfy ESI, CER, SPK, WRTD, SBS+, STEM+, and EXP+. ESE 301 satisfies STAS. One SBC must fulfill two objectives. SBC tags for individual courses are stored on course records.
